ostrzezenia.tekst: Almost any food that is not very acidic, with a pH above 4.6, can support the growth of Clostridium botulinum and toxin production.
According to the FDA, the minimum temperature for growth and toxin production by Clostridium botulinum type E and nonproteolytic types B and F is 38°F (3.3°C).

akapity: According to an FDA table of approximate values, beets have a pH of 4.9–5.6.
Beet is a vegetable, and all fresh vegetables except most tomatoes are low-acid foods with a pH above 4.6.
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe that uses red wine to acidify beet preserves.
